title: Graphics Card Payback: Renting Out vs Serving Models
tools: Python data pipeline · JavaScript calculator page · Vast.ai, OpenRouter, InferenceX and GetDeploying data
blurb: An interactive calculator for how many months a data-center GPU (graphics processing unit) takes to pay for itself, two ways: renting it out by the hour, or serving open models through OpenRouter. It covers 16 cards, 19 open models and 155 model-and-card pairs, built from live market prices and measured benchmarks.
long: The question: if you buy a large server GPU (graphics processing unit), how long until it pays for itself? The page compares two ways to earn: rent the card out by the hour on a marketplace, or run open-weight models on it and sell the output through OpenRouter, an API (application programming interface) marketplace for language models.

Python scripts pull Vast.ai rental offers, OpenRouter's per-provider token prices and traffic, InferenceX throughput benchmarks and GetDeploying weekly rental prices, plus a hand-kept catalogue of new and used purchase prices with sources. Server-board cards are priced as their 8-card server divided by 8 (racks by 72). Serving speed is the best measured throughput per card that still gives each user at least 30 tokens per second; rows without a direct benchmark borrow a similar model's speed and are marked as estimates.

Every assumption is a control: electricity price, rack-space cost, cooling overhead, share of hours rented, which rental price, marketplace fee, which token price, your share of a model's traffic, peak utilisation, and a yearly price drop. At the page's defaults (data as of 7 October 2026), the fastest rental payback is 17.1 months (a used H100 server board), and the fastest serving payback is 5.3 months (Kimi K3 on an AMD MI355X, a GPU), but serving income is capped by demand: the cheapest providers take most of the traffic.
A Node script runs the page's own calculation code on the data bundle to check its numbers outside the browser.
